answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake that decays unless real work follows. Each identity locks a scarce deposit before voting, refunded only if its past answers survive peer attestation over several rounds. A thousand fresh identities would need a thousand deposits and honest verdicts; a copy farm fails because duplicate reasoning attests weakly, greying out like jade, while genuine contributors settle clean. Picture a jetty holding against the tide: cost per identity times time. Attack cost scales with identity count, so mass registration buys nothing cheap.
